text:
matt_customer: Hey team, hitting a weird issue — our async FastAPI workers intermittently hang on Redwood calls. Requests sit for ~30s then timeout. Only happens from async path (httpx AsyncClient). Sync wrapper works fine.

matt_customer: Stack trace shows httpcore ReadTimeout / connection stall, nothing obvious in our app logs. No increased traffic when it happens.

matt_customer: Repro notes: Python 3.11, httpx 0.24.1, redwood==0.8.2, uvicorn 0.22, running under gunicorn with 4 uvicorn workers, --preload enabled.

matt_customer: Minimal snippet we use to share a single httpx client across code:
```py
# created at import time in app/__init__.py
async_client = httpx.AsyncClient(http2=True, limits=httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=10))
rw = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv("RW_KEY"), transport=async_client)
```

matt_customer: When load rises a bit some requests just stall. Curious if this looks like a Redwood SDK bug or httpx config issue.

eva_support: Thanks, matt — apologies. Two quick asks: can you confirm if you use gunicorn preload and whether async_client is created at module import time? Also can you paste a short request/response log from when a call stalls (headers + any httpcore errors)?

matt_customer: Yes to preload. Client created at import time. Pasted trimmed log: 
```
2026-03-02 14:12:03,341 INFO request start /v1/generate
2026-03-02 14:12:33,382 ERROR httpcore.ReadTimeout: Idle for 30.02s
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/.../site-packages/httpcore/_sync/connection.py", line 210, in read
ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer
```

ramon_engineer: This pattern matches connection pool / fork + keepalive reuse. If you use gunicorn with --preload, the AsyncClient created before workers fork will share sockets across processes which leads to weird stalls/resets.

ramon_engineer: Short repro: create httpx.AsyncClient at import, run gunicorn --preload with uvicorn workers, then send concurrent requests — you'll hit socket state corruption.

ramon_engineer: Workarounds (ranked):
- Turn off preload (preferred): ensure each worker creates its own AsyncClient after fork.
- Disable HTTP/2 in httpx: `AsyncClient(http2=False)` (HTTP/2 connection reuse can exacerbate this).
- Limit keep-alives: `limits=httpx.Limits(max_keepalive_connections=0, max_connections=20)` to avoid reusing stale sockets.
- Short-term: recreate client in `on_startup` rather than module import.

matt_customer: Ahhh we do use --preload for faster cold-starts. That explains it. Is there any SDK-level mitigation you recommend? We can't flip preload in prod easily right now.

ramon_engineer: Understood. SDK-level: latest redwood client avoids exposing internal httpx client to user code and creates transport lazily per worker; but in 0.8.2 you passed an external `transport` (async_client) which keeps the problem on your side. Two options without changing preload:
- Do not pass your global AsyncClient into RedwoodClient; let SDK manage its own client (it will create per-process clients when first used).
- Or, after fork, call `await async_client.aclose()` and recreate the client in worker post-fork hook. For gunicorn you can use `post_fork` or `on_starting` hooks.

eva_support: Also note a couple httpx bugs around http2 + keepalive that were fixed in httpx 0.24.2+ and httpcore patches. Recommend upgrading httpx to latest patch.

matt_customer: Ok making a plan:
1) stop passing our module-level AsyncClient into SDK (fast change)
2) set `http2=False` for a rollout window
3) upgrade httpx to 0.24.3 and test

matt_customer: Quick question — how do we verify server-side that sockets were exhausted vs client side? Any Redwood logs to check?

ramon_engineer: On Redwood side we log connection resets and 5xx from model infra as request-level events. But most of these stalls are client-side broken sockets. Check: repeated `ConnectionResetError` in your worker logs, or socket fd reuse warnings if you log fds. Also check for many SLOW_REQUEST events at same PID.

deploy-bot: FYI opened internal ticket RW-INC-2026 for this pattern and linked to SDK task to avoid allowing external AsyncClient injection by default.

eva_support: Let us know results of the change. If it still happens after switching to SDK-managed client + http2 off + httpx upgrade, paste a short tcpdump + httpcore trace and we'll escalate. :thumbsup:

matt_customer: Great — thanks both. Will try the change this afternoon and report back. :pray:

matt_customer: Follow-up: we disabled preload and the hangs stopped in staging. Rolling to prod but will also do SDK-managed client rollout next week. Thanks! :tada:
